file_roles.evidence: The entire change in QWindowsFontDatabase::populateFamily is the severity of one diagnostic plus a comment: 'qCWarning(lcQpaFonts) << "Unable to enumerate family '" << familyName << '\'';' becomes 'qCDebug(lcQpaFonts) << ...', with '// Field length of LOGFONT::lfFaceName' added to the unchanged guard 'if (familyName.size() >= LF_FACESIZE)'. The guard and the 'return;' behave exactly as before.

rationale: The reported line 'qt.qpa.fonts: Unable to enumerate family " Droid Sans Mono Dotted for Powerline "' is the literal text of the qCWarning in populateFamily, and its category tag places it there. Nothing the function does was corrected: the LF_FACESIZE guard and the early return are untouched, and only the logging level drops to qCDebug, which is why the commit says 'Turn the warning into a qCDebug() statement and add explanatory comment'. Under the convention that symptom-handling covers a change that only reports, where the production code was right and nothing it does was corrected, this is symptom-handling and the instance has no causal file.
notes: The instance has no failure: a font family name longer than LF_FACESIZE cannot be enumerated through LOGFONT, which is a platform limit rather than a bug, and the complaint is log noise. A second rater would reasonably disagree and call this causal, since the warning is itself the reported problem and the only changed line is that warning; it is labelled symptom-handling because the rubric reserves causal for logic that was wrong and the diff corrects no behaviour. Worth putting in the agreement check. The fix ships with no regression test.
